title: New Research Offers Hope for Earlier Bowel Disease Detection
subtitle: Scientists find immune system warning signs up to a decade before symptoms appear.

summary.en: Recent studies suggest that inflammatory bowel disease can be predicted years before diagnosis. Researchers identified specific antibodies in the blood that act as early warning signs. This discovery could change how doctors treat Crohn’s disease and ulcerative colitis. Currently, patients often receive treatment only after significant damage has occurred. Experts hope this leads to future prevention strategies similar to those used for other immune conditions.
summary.zh: 近期研究顯示，發炎性腸道疾病在確診前數年即可預測。研究人員在血液中發現了可作為早期預警訊號的特定抗體。這項發現可能改變醫生治療克隆氏症與潰瘍性結腸炎的方式。目前，患者往往在病情已造成顯著損害後才接受治療。專家希望此發現能引領未來採取類似其他免疫疾病的預防策略。

paragraphs.en: Following our previous report on early warning signs for bowel disease, new research has provided a clearer picture of how inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) develops. Scientists have discovered that the immune system sends out specific warning signals up to a decade before a person is officially diagnosed. This finding is a major step forward in understanding a condition that affects at least 3.8 million people worldwide.
paragraphs.zh: 繼我們之前關於腸道疾病早期預警徵兆的報導後，一項新研究更清晰地呈現了發炎性腸道疾病（IBD）的發展過程。科學家發現，免疫系統在患者正式確診前十年，就會發出特定的預警訊號。這項發現對於理解這種影響全球至少三百八十萬人的疾病，是一項重大的進展。

paragraphs.en: According to The Guardian Health, the two main forms of IBD—Crohn’s disease and ulcerative colitis—are usually treated only after a patient starts feeling sick. By this time, the digestive tract has often already suffered damage. Dr. Arno Bourgonje, a researcher at the University Medical Centre Groningen and the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai, explained that for many patients, treatment currently starts too late. The new study shows that the disease process begins years before the first symptoms appear, leaving clear signs in the blood that doctors might one day be able to track.
paragraphs.zh: 根據《衛報健康版》（The Guardian Health）報導，發炎性腸道疾病的兩種主要形式——克隆氏症與潰瘍性結腸炎，通常要等到患者開始感到不適後才會進行治療。到了這個階段，消化道往往已經受損。格羅寧根大學醫學中心（University Medical Centre Groningen）與西奈山伊坎醫學院（Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai）的研究員阿諾·布爾貢傑博士（Dr. Arno Bourgonje）解釋，對許多患者而言，目前的治療開始得太晚。這項新研究顯示，疾病過程在首發症狀出現前數年就已開始，並在血液中留下醫生未來或許能追蹤的明確跡象。

paragraphs.en: To reach these findings, researchers studied blood samples from 500 US military personnel. They looked closely at 200 people who later developed Crohn’s disease and 200 who developed ulcerative colitis. By screening these samples, the team identified specific antibodies—proteins produced by the immune system to fight off things like bacteria or viruses—that were present long before the illness started. In those who developed Crohn’s disease, researchers found more antibodies related to the Epstein-Barr virus, which is known for causing glandular fever. Those who developed ulcerative colitis showed a different pattern, including antibodies that reacted against the body’s own proteins.
paragraphs.zh: 為了得出這些發現，研究人員分析了五百名美國軍事人員的血液樣本。他們仔細觀察了其中兩百名後來罹患克隆氏症的人，以及兩百名罹患潰瘍性結腸炎的人。透過篩檢這些樣本，研究團隊辨識出特定的抗體——即免疫系統為對抗細菌或病毒等外來物所產生的蛋白質——這些抗體在疾病發作前很久就已存在。在罹患克隆氏症的患者體內，研究人員發現了更多與愛潑斯坦-巴爾病毒（Epstein-Barr virus）相關的抗體，該病毒以引發腺熱聞名。而罹患潰瘍性結腸炎的患者則呈現出不同的模式，包括對人體自身蛋白質產生反應的抗體。

paragraphs.en: These results were recently shared at the United European Gastroenterology meeting in Barcelona and published in the journal Gut. While the study is promising, experts note that it currently shows a link rather than proof that these infections directly cause IBD. The research team emphasized that this is not yet a test that can tell someone for certain that they will become ill. Instead, it is a foundation for future work that could allow doctors to catch the disease much earlier.
paragraphs.zh: 這些結果近期在巴塞隆納舉行的聯合歐洲胃腸病學會議（United European Gastroenterology meeting）上分享，並發表於《腸道》（Gut）期刊。儘管這項研究前景看好，但專家指出，目前僅顯示出兩者之間的關聯，而非證明這些感染直接導致了發炎性腸道疾病。研究團隊強調，這還不是一項能確切告知某人未來一定會發病的檢測，而是為未來的研究奠定基礎，讓醫生有機會更早發現疾病。

paragraphs.en: Why does this matter? Currently, treatment for IBD relies on anti-inflammatory drugs—medicines that reduce swelling and irritation—and immune-suppressing drugs, which lower the activity of the immune system. Unfortunately, many patients do not respond well to these treatments, and some eventually require surgery to remove damaged parts of the bowel. Furthermore, long-term inflammation in the gut increases the risk of developing bowel cancer. By identifying people at risk before the damage begins, doctors hope to change the future of care.
paragraphs.zh: 為什麼這很重要？目前，發炎性腸道疾病的治療依賴抗發炎藥物（用於減輕腫脹與刺激的藥物）以及免疫抑制劑（用於降低免疫系統活性）。遺憾的是，許多患者對這些治療反應不佳，有些人最終需要透過手術切除受損的腸道部位。此外，腸道長期發炎會增加罹患腸癌的風險。透過在損害發生前辨識出高風險族群，醫生希望能改變未來的照護模式。

paragraphs.en: James Lindsay, a professor of gastroenterology at Barts Health, noted that the study provides important insights into the causes of Crohn’s disease. He and other experts are hopeful that IBD could eventually follow the path of type 1 diabetes. In the case of diabetes, doctors can use blood tests to identify people whose immune systems have begun attacking the pancreas before any symptoms appear. This early identification allows for treatments that can delay the onset of the disease.
paragraphs.zh: 巴茲健康中心（Barts Health）的胃腸病學教授詹姆斯·林賽（James Lindsay）指出，這項研究為克隆氏症的成因提供了重要見解。他與其他專家都希望，發炎性腸道疾病最終能循著第一型糖尿病的模式發展。在糖尿病的案例中，醫生可以利用血液檢測，在任何症狀出現前，找出免疫系統已開始攻擊胰臟的患者。這種早期辨識能讓醫療團隊採取治療，進而延緩疾病的發作。

paragraphs.en: Looking ahead, the research team says the findings must be confirmed in other groups of people to ensure the results are accurate across different populations. While there is still much work to be done, the ability to see the disease coming years in advance offers a new sense of optimism. If scientists can successfully turn these warning signs into a reliable screening tool, it could prevent years of pain and serious health complications for millions of people around the world.
paragraphs.zh: 展望未來，研究團隊表示，這些發現必須在其他群體中進行驗證，以確保結果在不同族群間皆準確。雖然還有許多工作要做，但能提前數年預見疾病的能力，帶來了一種新的樂觀情緒。如果科學家能成功將這些預警訊號轉化為可靠的篩檢工具，將能為全球數百萬人免去多年的痛苦與嚴重的健康併發症。

previousArticles.title: New Research Shows Early Warning Signs for Bowel Disease
previousArticles.summaryEn: Researchers have found that the immune system shows warning signs up to ten years before a diagnosis of inflammatory bowel disease. By studying blood samples, scientists identified specific antibodies that appear long before symptoms start. This discovery could change how doctors treat conditions like Crohn’s disease and ulcerative colitis. Currently, these diseases are often treated only after significant damage to the gut has already occurred. Experts hope this research will eventually lead to early prevention and better health outcomes for patients.

quiz.question: What specific biological difference was observed in the blood samples of those who later developed Crohn’s disease compared to those who developed ulcerative colitis?

options.A: They had lower levels of immune-suppressing proteins.
options.B: They showed a higher presence of antibodies linked to the Epstein-Barr virus.
options.C: They lacked the antibodies that react against the body's own proteins.
options.D: They exhibited signs of damage to the digestive tract long before the others.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第三段，研究人員在後來患有克隆氏症（Crohn’s disease）的樣本中，發現了更多與愛潑斯坦-巴爾病毒（Epstein-Barr virus）相關的抗體。選項 A 文章未提及；選項 C 描述的是潰瘍性結腸炎（ulcerative colitis）患者的特徵，而非克隆氏症；選項 D 雖然提到損害，但文章指出損害是在出現症狀後才明顯，並非血液樣本中的抗體差異。

quiz.question: Based on the comparisons made in the article, what is the primary reason researchers are optimistic about the future of IBD treatment?

options.A: They have already developed a cure that prevents the disease entirely.
options.B: They believe that anti-inflammatory drugs will soon be replaced by surgery.
options.C: They hope to replicate the early detection success seen in managing type 1 diabetes.
options.D: They have confirmed that the Epstein-Barr virus is the sole cause of all bowel diseases.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。文章第六段提到，專家希望發炎性腸道疾病（IBD）能遵循第一型糖尿病的模式，透過血液檢測在症狀出現前識別免疫系統的攻擊，從而延緩發病。選項 A 錯誤，因為研究目前僅是基礎階段；選項 B 錯誤，因為目標是減少對手術的需求；選項 D 錯誤，因為文章第四段強調這只是關聯性而非直接的因果證明。

quiz.question: In the final paragraph, what does the phrase 'turn these warning signs into a reliable screening tool' imply?

options.A: Converting biological data into a practical method for early disease detection.
options.B: Physically changing the appearance of the warning signs in the blood.
options.C: Replacing medical doctors with automated diagnostic machines.
options.D: Creating a new medication that masks the symptoms of the disease.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。在此語境中，「turn... into」意指將研究發現的生物標記（警告訊號）轉化為實際可用的臨床檢測手段（screening tool）。選項 B 是對「turn」的字面誤解；選項 C 超出了文章範圍，文章強調的是醫生的應用而非取代；選項 D 錯誤，因為檢測工具的目的在於識別風險，而非遮蓋症狀。

quiz.question: What is the central message of the article?

options.A: The Epstein-Barr virus is the primary cause of all digestive system failures.
options.B: Current IBD treatments are highly effective if started within a decade of diagnosis.
options.C: New research suggests that early identification of immune signals could transform IBD management.
options.D: US military personnel are the only group at risk of developing inflammatory bowel disease.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。全文的核心在於介紹一項新研究，該研究發現免疫系統在發炎性腸道疾病（IBD）確診前十年就會發出訊號，這為未來更早期的診斷與治療提供了希望。選項 A 過度概括；選項 B 與文章提到「治療太晚」的觀點矛盾；選項 D 錯誤，研究僅是使用軍人樣本作為研究對象，而非僅限該群體患病。
